title: "11. Remote computing"
---

```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(dMod2)
# the local job runs in an empty folder, where it finds no shared objects of other articles
.work <- tempfile("remote-computing-")
dir.create(.work)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = .work)
.outdir <- options(dMod2.outdir = NULL)
```

Conditions of one evaluation run in threads, independent fits and
[profiles](methods-profiles.html#def-profile) in processes.
`distributedComputing()` runs R code as tasks in detached processes, locally, over ssh or as a
SLURM array job. Only the local job below runs at page build.

## Threads and processes

`options(dMod2.cores = n)`, or `obj(pars, cores = n)` for one call, solves the conditions of an
evaluation in `n` OpenMP threads inside cppDE; a single condition uses one.

`mstrust()`, `msem()` and `profile()` run fits as processes through `cores`. With one number, fits
are forks of the session with one thread each. `cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2)` runs four fits
with two threads each in fresh R processes (a PSOCK cluster, always on Windows). Memory grows with
the process count; keep the product of both below the core count.

| where | argument | axis |
|---|---|---|
| one evaluation | `options(dMod2.cores = )`, `obj(pars, cores = )` | conditions, threads |
| `em()` | `cores` | groups and conditions, threads |
| `mstrust()`, `msem()` | `cores`, `c(fits = , conditions = )` | fits, processes |
| `profile()` | `cores`, `c(pars = , conditions = )` | parameters, processes |
| `distributedComputing()` | `tasks`, `on` | tasks, detached processes |

```{r}
options(dMod2.cores = 2)
fits <- mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 20,
                cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2))
profiles <- profile(obj, best, names(best), fixed = gauge, cores = 8)
```

## Tasks and job code

`distributedComputing(expr, tasks, on)` evaluates `expr` once per task in a fresh R process; the
value is the task result. `tasks` is a count, a list or vector with one element per task, or a
data frame with one row per task. Inside `expr`:

- `task`: the element or row (as a list, `task$n`), `NULL` when `tasks` is a count,
- `taskId`: the position in `tasks`,
- `cores`: cores available to the task, e.g. for `mstrust(cores = cores)`,
  `parallel::mclapply(mc.cores = cores)` or `options(dMod2.cores = cores)`,
- `jobname`: the job name.

`input` names the session objects the code reads, by default all objects of the calling
environment. The process attaches dMod2 and the R defaults; session options do not reach it.

Example: coverage of the 95% t interval for exponential samples, one task per sample size:

```{r coverage, eval = TRUE}
interval <- function(y) t.test(y)$conf.int
sizes <- data.frame(n = c(5, 10, 20, 50))
job <- distributedComputing(
  {
    message("task ", taskId, ": samples of size ", task$n)
    covered <- replicate(2000, {
      ci <- interval(rexp(task$n))
      ci[1] < 1 && 1 < ci[2]
    })
    data.frame(n = task$n, coverage = mean(covered))
  },
  tasks = sizes, on = localNode(cores = 1), jobname = "coverage", input = "interval", seed = 1
)
job
```

The call returns once tasks have started. `job` is a list of functions:

```{r follow, eval = TRUE}
job$check()
job$wait(interval = 1)
job$get()
```

Task `i` uses seed `seed + i`. A task that errors returns the `try-error`, the others go on.

## Job folder layout

The job files go to `<jobname>_folder/<k>` in the home directory of node `k`, on `"localhost"`
in the working directory. The local `<jobname>_folder` also holds the manifest `job.rds`:

```{r folder, eval = TRUE}
list.files("coverage_folder", recursive = TRUE)
```

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `workspace.RData` | objects of `input`; `zstd`-compressed when available locally |
| `tasks.rds` | tasks as a list, one entry per data frame row |
| `job.R` | R script of a task |
| model files | sources, objects or shared objects, see [Model files and builds](#model-files-and-builds) |
| `build.sh`, `files.txt`, `build.log` | model build on the node, build output |
| `slot_<k>.sh`, `.pid`, `.run` | runner script of node `k`, process ID of the script and of the running task |
| `job.sh`, `env.sh` | SLURM only: job script from the template, job environment |
| `task_<i>.out`, `task_<i>.rds` | output and result of task `i` |

Every task runs `Rscript job.R <taskId> <cores>`:

```{r jobscript, eval = TRUE}
writeLines(readLines("coverage_folder/1/job.R"))
```

The code runs in the job folder of the node; files written there come back with
`get(all = TRUE)`.

## Nodes and workers

`on` says where tasks run:

```{r}
on <- localNode()                                        # the local machine, with the free cores
on <- localNode(cores = 8)
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"))                  # each node with the free cores there
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"), cores = 10)
on <- sshNodes(cores = c(server1 = 24, server2 = 20))
on <- sshNodes(c("localhost", "server1"))                # the local machine and one more
on <- slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 8, walltime = "12:00:00")
```

A node is an ssh destination (`"host"`, `"user@host"`) with key authentication. `"localhost"`
runs without ssh, with the R and library paths of the session; `localNode()` is
`sshNodes("localhost")`.

Each node is one worker. Task `i` goes to worker `(i - 1) %% W + 1` of `W`; a worker runs the
assigned tasks in sequence with the `cores` of the node. `tasks = NULL`, the default, gives one
task per worker. `cores` is one number, a vector named by node, or `NULL` for the free cores,
which `detectFreeCores()` counts as cores minus the load average.

```{r}
detectFreeCores(c("localhost", "server1", "server2"))
```

Tasks survive the end of the ssh connection and the session, and run with
`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1` and `libs` first in the library paths.

## Model files and builds

The model files of a job are those of the model objects in `input`; without any, all model
files of `getOption("dMod2.outdir")`, else of the working directory. `build`:

- `"compile"`: sources are compiled on the node into one shared object against the cppDE
  installed there, with `buildCores` compilers (default the node cores, at most 16) and
  `buildBundle` sources per translation unit.
- `"link"`: object files are copied and linked, which needs a compatible compiler on the node.
- `"copy"`: shared objects are copied, which needs a compatible node.
- `"auto"`, the default: `"copy"` when all nodes are `"localhost"`, else `"compile"`.

The build runs once per node, on SLURM once on the login node. A failed build stops the
submission and shows the end of `build.log`. `libs` prepends library paths on the nodes; `~` is the
remote home.

## Job monitoring and recovery

| function | does |
|---|---|
| `check()` | counts done, running, failed; `TRUE` once none runs, warns on failures |
| `wait(interval = 10)` | polls until none runs, reports changes; `TRUE` if all done |
| `get(combine = TRUE, all = FALSE)` | returns the results |
| `log(i, lines = 20)` | last output lines of task `i` |
| `purge(local = FALSE)` | deletes the job folders on the nodes, on `"localhost"` the local `<jobname>_folder/<k>`, with `local = TRUE` also local folder and registry entry |
| `terminate()` | stops the tasks |

A task is failed when the worker ended without a result. `get()` copies remote results into the
local `<jobname>_folder/<k>`, with `all = TRUE` all files. It joins parlists with `c()` and data
frames with `rbind()`, which merges the two sides of a profile; other results come as a list.
`get(combine = FALSE)` returns one entry per task: `NULL` if not done, the `try-error` if failed.

Output of the second task, then deletion:

```{r purge, eval = TRUE}
job$log(2)
job$purge(local = TRUE)
```

`distributedComputing(wait = TRUE)` waits, returns `get()` and deletes the job; a job with failed
tasks is kept for `log()`.

A job outlives the session. The manifest is in the local and remote `<jobname>_folder` and in
the registry `tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "data")`; `dMod2Jobs()` lists registered jobs.
`recover = TRUE` with a job name returns the job functions without resubmitting, from the working
directory, the registry or, with `on`, the remote nodes, also for a job from another machine. A
new job of the same name is an error while the old one runs in the same folders.

```{r}
dMod2Jobs()
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", recover = TRUE)
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")),
                            recover = TRUE)
```

## SLURM clusters

`slurmCluster()` names the login node and the resources per array task: `cores`, `walltime`,
`memPerCore` in GB. Workers are the `array` array tasks, by default one per task. The job folder
is `~/<jobname>_folder/1` on the login node, where the model files are built once and `sbatch`
submits, so compute nodes must see that home directory. `partition`, `account`, `maxRunning` and
`sbatch` (further options) override the `#SBATCH` lines of the template.

`slurmTemplate()` sets up the job script template once per login node. A template is a job
script with placeholders `{{ jobname }}`, `{{ ntasks }}`, `{{ cores }}`, `{{ memPerCore }}`,
`{{ walltime }}` and one line `{{ run }}`; lines before `{{ run }}` set up the environment, also
for the build. The shipped template for the bwForCluster Helix:

```{r template, eval = TRUE}
writeLines(readLines(system.file("slurm", "helix.sh", package = "dMod2")))
```

```{r}
slurmTemplate("mycluster", from = "~/mycluster.sh")   # once, from a job script, for editing
slurmTemplate("helix")                                 # the template dMod2 ships for Helix
slurmTemplate()                                        # the templates set up
cluster <- slurmCluster("helix", cores = 1, walltime = "12:00:00")
```

`slurmCluster(jobscript = )` takes another template for one job.

## Fits and profiles of the guide project

The 200 fits of [Optimization](guide-optimization.html) as 200 one-fit tasks:

```{r}
free <- setdiff(names(mu), names(gauge))
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 1, iterlim = 1000, tolControl = tolerances),
  tasks = 200, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "sigma", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
fitsJob$check()
fitsJob$wait(interval = 60)
fits <- as.parframe(fitsJob$get())
fitsJob$purge(local = TRUE)
```

A later session takes up the job by name:

```{r}
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(jobname = "oppelt_fits", recover = TRUE)
```

The profiles of [Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html), one side of one parameter per task;
`get()` binds both sides into one profile:

```{r}
sides <- expand.grid(par = names(best), side = c("left", "right"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
profilesJob <- distributedComputing(
  profile(obj, best, task$par, side = task$side, fixed = gauge,
          limits = c(lower = -7, upper = 7), stepControl = list(stop = "data"),
          optControl = list(iterlim = 100, tolControl = tolerances)),
  tasks = sides, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_profiles",
  input = c("obj", "best", "gauge", "tolerances"))
profilesJob$wait(interval = 60)
profiles <- profilesJob$get()
```

An `msem()` multistart splits by `which`: every task draws all starts from the same seed and fits
those it names. The 200 starts of [Sparse deviations](guide-sparse-deviations.html):

```{r}
dcfJob <- distributedComputing({
  set.seed(3)
  msem(objSS, randomSS, c(initDCF, prob_compound = 0.2, tau_compound = 0.5),
       fixed = gaugeReduced, fits = 200, sd = 0.5, keepFits = TRUE, which = task)
}, tasks = as.list(1:200), on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_dcf",
input = c("objSS", "randomSS", "initDCF", "gaugeReduced"))
fitDCF <- dcfJob$get()
```

`get()` returns the best `msem()` fit with all starts. Over ssh, one task per node:

```{r}
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 10 * cores, iterlim = 1000,
          tolControl = tolerances, cores = cores),
  on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")), jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "sigma", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
```

[Bile acid transport](bileAcidTransport.html) runs the multistarts as a local job,
[Kok 2020](kokMSB2020.html) the 200 fits as a SLURM array job.

## System requirements

- A POSIX shell locally (on Windows the `sh` of Rtools) and on every remote node, bash on remote
  nodes for `build = "compile"` (default) and `"link"`.
- Remote nodes: ssh with key authentication, dMod2 and cppDE for the R on the node `PATH` or in
  `libs`, a compiler for `build = "compile"`.
- SLURM: an account on the login node, a template from `slurmTemplate()`, a home directory visible
  to the compute nodes.
- `zstd` on every remote node if the local machine has it, since it then compresses the workspace.

Reference: `distributedComputing()`, `localNode()`, `sshNodes()`, `slurmCluster()`,
`slurmTemplate()`, `detectFreeCores()`, `dMod2Jobs()`, `mstrust()`, `msem()`, `profile()`
